title: Quantum Circuit Synthesis Using an Exact T Library
extraction_scope: Selected HTML sections 4.2–4.3 and 6; PDF page 6 Figures 8–11 visually inspected

pdf_verification.method: Local PyMuPDF 2x rendering and same-agent visual inspection

figure_8.limit: Section 6.2 ambiguously associates 14.3 percent with library-only mapping; chart assigns it to the bilinear mapper. Preserve chart attribution and flag prose discrepancy.

figure_9_counterexample.interpretation: Regression, not a uniform space-time improvement; values transcribed from labels, not inferred bar heights.

findings: C++ implementation, EPFL inputs and correctness fixtures are present; not a README-only artifact.
Verification harness invokes srun with batch partition and low qos; README's local command needs that environment or a documented adaptation.
Simulator checks basis-state outputs and probability above 0.99; it does not check relative phases across superpositions.

smoke_test.limits: No simulation or equivalence check executed; no benchmark metric reproduced. Temporary output location must be replaced when rerunning.

conditions.finding: Six EPFL arithmetic circuits; comparison against exact-MC mapping; customized mapper reports 5.3 percent geomean T-count reduction.
Library-only substitution reports about 0.5 percent geomean reduction and regressions on some circuits.
Exact solver bound is N <= 7 total qubits, not seven arbitrary logical inputs; larger instances use suboptimal solutions.
Correctness assumes clean output ancilla initialized to zero; not unrestricted unitary equivalence.
Mapping stages account for at most 11.7 percent of total synthesis runtime in the reported QLUT evaluation.

interpretation_limits: T-count savings are not measured hardware speedup or universal space-time savings.
Do not promote small-library exactness into whole-circuit global optimality.
Resolve source-version discrepancy before retaining a headline; chart labels are source claims, not reproduced measurements.
Pinned code availability does not establish benchmark reproduction, phase-correctness, proof validity or independent acceptance.
